# The wordings of naturalloy

<!-- generated by `node test/core/wordings.ts --write`; edits are overwritten -->

Each pass changes how a statement is said, and never what it means: the analyzer is asked of every change a pass makes to the IR of the sweep. With every pass off, the printer says the literal reading. A pass is shown here with the shortest statement of the sweep it changes, as it reads with that pass off and with every pass on.

## negation-inward

Spec: [`spec-not-before-a-compound-is-said-with-the-not-moved-inward`](CANON.md#spec-not-before-a-compound-is-said-with-the-not-moved-inward). It changes 115 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
all c: Cleanup, o, p: Owner | not o in Cleanup.on
```

Off:

```text
For every cleanup_1, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  it is not the case that:
    a cleanup is on owner_1.
```

On:

```text
For every cleanup_1, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  no cleanup is on owner_1.
```

## exactly-one

Spec: [`spec-not-before-an-equivalence-is-said-as-exactly-one-of-its-sides`](CANON.md#spec-not-before-an-equivalence-is-said-as-exactly-one-of-its-sides). It changes 30 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
all c: Cleanup, o, p: Owner | not (c in Ran iff o in Disposed)
```

Off:

```text
For every cleanup, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  it is not the case that:
    the cleanup has run exactly when pulse has disposed owner_1.
```

On:

```text
For every cleanup, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  exactly one of these holds:
    - the cleanup has run
    - pulse has disposed owner_1
```

## always-inside-for-every

Spec: [`spec-a-rule-at-every-later-moment-is-said-from-now-on-whenever`](CANON.md#spec-a-rule-at-every-later-moment-is-said-from-now-on-whenever). It changes 7 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
always all c: Cleanup | c in Registered implies c in Ran
```

Off:

```text
From now on, for every cleanup:
  when code has registered the cleanup, the cleanup has run.
```

On:

```text
For every cleanup:
  from now on, whenever code has registered the cleanup, the cleanup has run.
```

## x-and-no-other

Spec: [`spec-a-set-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-as-the-variable-and-no-other`](CANON.md#spec-a-set-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-as-the-variable-and-no-other). It changes 22 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
all c: Cleanup, s: String | c.tags = "a"
```

Off:

```text
For every cleanup, every text_1 and every text_2:
  the cleanup is tagged text_2 exactly when text_2 and "a" are the same.
```

On:

```text
For every cleanup and every text_1:
  the cleanup is tagged "a" and is tagged no other text.
```

- Readers: A strict judge (Opus) found 46 of 46 changed statements lossless; two haiku readers got 16 of 16 situations right, "no other" over an empty set among them.
- Rejected: "no other" inside a noun phrase, as in "an owner that no other owner is the parent of": it covers less than the claim.
- Rejected: a field of at most one value: its reading already says it, "owner_1 is the home of the cleanup".

## for-every-together

Spec: [`spec-a-for-every-right-inside-a-for-every-is-one-for-every`](CANON.md#spec-a-for-every-right-inside-a-for-every-is-one-for-every). It changes 187 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
all c: Cleanup, o, p: Owner | all x: Owner | x in Stopped
```

Off:

```text
For every cleanup, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  for every owner_3:
    the dispose of owner_3 has been stopped.
```

On:

```text
For every cleanup, every owner_1, every owner_2 and every owner_3:
  the dispose of owner_3 has been stopped.
```

## another-of-a-kind

Spec: [`spec-a-variable-that-must-differ-from-another-of-its-kind-is-said-as-another`](CANON.md#spec-a-variable-that-must-differ-from-another-of-its-kind-is-said-as-another). It changes 0 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

## noun-phrases

Spec: [`spec-a-variable-said-once-takes-the-place-of-its-quantifier-as-a-noun-phrase`](CANON.md#spec-a-variable-said-once-takes-the-place-of-its-quantifier-as-a-noun-phrase). It changes 150 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
some c: Cleanup, o: Owner | o in c.on and o in Disposed
```

Off:

```text
There is a cleanup that is on an owner that pulse has disposed.
```

On:

```text
A cleanup is on an owner that pulse has disposed.
```

- Rejected: "another" where the formula has no "!=".
- Rejected: a noun phrase hanging only from another noun phrase, "a cleanup is on an owner": it reads as said of every cleanup.

## definition-by-kinds

Spec: [`spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-for-each-kind`](CANON.md#spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-for-each-kind). It changes 0 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

## there-is-a-that

Spec: [`spec-a-quantifier-about-its-variable-alone-is-said-with-there-is-and-that`](CANON.md#spec-a-quantifier-about-its-variable-alone-is-said-with-there-is-and-that). It changes 0 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

- Readers: A strict judge (Opus) found 46 of 46 changed statements lossless; two haiku readers judged 16 situations each and got all of them right.
- Readers: For the bullets after "that:", two haiku readers and one sonnet reader judged 7 situations each and got all of them right, including one list meeting some conditions and another the rest.
- Rejected: "a unit is a spec": reads as said of every unit.
- Rejected: "no claim takes no lane": a double negative.
- Rejected: bullets after "there is no unit that:": each bullet could read as denied on its own.
- Rejected: "there is a list that has three clauses or fewer, has an item that holds a comma and has more than two clauses": the relative clause "that holds a comma" can run over what follows it.

## until-in-a-sentence

Spec: [`spec-until-of-two-plain-clauses-is-one-sentence`](CANON.md#spec-until-of-two-plain-clauses-is-one-sentence). It changes 40 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
all c: Cleanup, o, p: Owner | (c in Ran until o in Disposed)
```

Off:

```text
For every cleanup, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  all of these hold:
    - now or later, the following holds:
        pulse has disposed owner_1
    - at every moment from now until the first such moment, not including it, the following holds:
        the cleanup has run.
```

On:

```text
For every cleanup, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  pulse has disposed owner_1 now or later, and until then, the cleanup has run.
```

- Readers: On 8 timelines built to catch each misreading, 5 of 5 readers (Opus, Sonnet, three haiku) read "until then" right; "first" is not needed, since any moment of b gives the same truth.
- Rejected: "up to the first such moment, but not necessarily at it": lossless, and longer than it needs to be.
- Rejected: "ever since", "since then" and "after that" for since: each misread by a haiku reader, as counting the moment of b itself or as its first moment; since needs the last.

## time-phrase-in-front

Spec: [`spec-a-time-phrase-before-words-that-hold-a-time-phrase-sets-them-apart`](CANON.md#spec-a-time-phrase-before-words-that-hold-a-time-phrase-sets-them-apart). It changes 346 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
always all c: Cleanup | c in Ran
```

Off:

```text
From now on:
  for every cleanup:
    the cleanup has run.
```

On:

```text
From now on, for every cleanup:
  the cleanup has run.
```

## clauses-in-a-sentence

Spec: [`spec-three-clauses-or-fewer-are-said-in-a-sentence`](CANON.md#spec-three-clauses-or-fewer-are-said-in-a-sentence). It changes 385 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
all c: Cleanup, o, p: Owner | let s = c.on | o in s and c in Ran
```

Off:

```text
For every cleanup, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  all of these hold:
    - the cleanup is on owner_1
    - the cleanup has run
```

On:

```text
For every cleanup, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  the cleanup is on owner_1 and has run.
```

## exactly-when

Spec: [`spec-an-equivalence-of-two-clauses-is-said-with-exactly-when`](CANON.md#spec-an-equivalence-of-two-clauses-is-said-with-exactly-when). It changes 40 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
all c: Cleanup, o, p: Owner | (c in Ran iff o in Disposed)
```

Off:

```text
For every cleanup, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  both or neither of these hold:
    - the cleanup has run
    - pulse has disposed owner_1
```

On:

```text
For every cleanup, every owner_1 and every owner_2:
  the cleanup has run exactly when pulse has disposed owner_1.
```

## rule-on-one-line

Spec: [`spec-a-rule-of-two-clauses-is-said-on-one-line`](CANON.md#spec-a-rule-of-two-clauses-is-said-on-one-line). It changes 261 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
always all c: Cleanup | c in Registered implies c in Ran
```

Off:

```text
For every cleanup:
  from now on, whenever code has registered the cleanup
  then the cleanup has run.
```

On:

```text
For every cleanup:
  from now on, whenever code has registered the cleanup, the cleanup has run.
```

## from-now-on-whenever

Spec: [`spec-a-rule-at-every-later-moment-is-said-from-now-on-whenever`](CANON.md#spec-a-rule-at-every-later-moment-is-said-from-now-on-whenever). It changes 8 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
always all c: Cleanup | c in Registered implies c in Ran
```

Off:

```text
For every cleanup:
  from now on:
    when code has registered the cleanup, the cleanup has run.
```

On:

```text
For every cleanup:
  from now on, whenever code has registered the cleanup, the cleanup has run.
```

- Readers: Two passes of a strict judge (Opus) found 98 of 102 sampled statements lossless; the 4 failures came from the old "a moment before", now "a moment just before".
- Readers: On a canon of 41 rules, a judge rated 25 as reading as well as the handwritten claim, against none before.
- Rejected: "whenever" over a rule that says "now" or a moment before: its "now" would count from each moment "whenever" picks.

Spec: [`spec-a-variable-alone-of-its-noun-is-named-the-noun`](CANON.md#spec-a-variable-alone-of-its-noun-is-named-the-noun). It changes 1419 of the 1737 formulas of the sweep.

```alloy
always all c: Cleanup | c in Ran
```
